utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bucko. May I remind you of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies. Now, I think Mr. Domazet has got a few more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Domazet: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning, Your Honours, good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bucko.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You must remember that you gave a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal quite a number of years ago.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, back in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took an oath and that's that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I take it that your statement was truthful and that you only told the truth?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the truth only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree that back in 1995, ten years ago, your recollection was much more vivid than it might be today?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was younger back then. I'm older now. So my memory, too, is slightly weaker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know, I'm sure, that your wife gave such a statement and she testified before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course she had to give a statement since we live in the same house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You've been married for a long time?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you know your wife very well. My question: Would she have any reason at all not to tell the truth to this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have been married for 43 years. I suppose we trust each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I take your answer to mean that you believe there is no reason for her not to be telling the truth to this Tribunal about anything and especially about you?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: She would have had no reason at all to tell anything else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you spoke about your area, the area in which you lived, being a mixed area. More than half the families in your area were Serb families?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said then, and I'm asking you now, that you had had a peaceful and good coexistence with all your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Court to provide a lengthier explanation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my questions only.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm trying to answer your question, precisely what you asked me. I'm trying to tell you about how we lived. We lived side by side, as brothers. We went our separate ways, that's true, but there are those who saw me off when I had to go and took me back and there are those who left and there are those who are still there and we still live together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's go back to a time before the war. You said most of your neighbours started leaving Vukovar, specifically because they knew, you said, that something would happen. Can you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's very simple. When they heard about Borovo Selo they knew right away that they had certain suspicions and that's why they did what they did. Nobody drove them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, and I hope you will now confirm, or deny, that they were telling you that they felt they were in danger and were afraid to remain in Vukovar with the Croats. That's from your statement.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one man said one thing and the next man said something different altogether. One neighbour told me this, the other neighbour told me that. One neighbour told me, "I sent my wife and both my children to Belgrade and gave them each a thousand Deutschmark." That's what he told me. I don't know what the case really was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was a question about barricades yesterday. We are done with that. But I want to know, did you hear at the time about explosions in Vukovar, houses being set on fire, and newspaper kiosk being blown up? Did you hear about any of that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to anyone. I didn't see anything myself, but people were saying all sorts of things, but I wasn't there. I didn't hear anything, and I had no idea whose houses they set fire to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that for the most part you moved within your family up and down your street except for those times when you drove your wife to work and back?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I went to visit every time I could. I went to the hospital whenever I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the 25th of August, that day, the day you saw planes flying over Vukovar. Can you please remember if the day before you heard a single plane being shot down above Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was born on the 24th of August so I remember well. We were in our house and we went out to watch the planes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think I understand your answer. I don't think that answers my question.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll repeat it for you. You're asking me about earlier on, the 24th, for example, which happens to be my birthday. We were in my house, I watched the planes flying overhead, and I know where they were coming from, from the Danube towards Bogdanovci, and they were flying fast above Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're saying you saw planes on the 24th but it was on the 25th that they actually bombed Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but 24th -- the 24th was the date when the first plane came. The 24th was the day when they started throwing grenades and bombs dropping them on Vukovar, whatever, give or take a day or two. I don't think that matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, I am trying --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're trying to cheat me, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to be specific. You said that Vukovar was bombed from planes on the 25th and not the 24th, is that true?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your answer I also hear that there were planes flying over Vukovar on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were flying overhead all the time. I was -- I was not the pilot of those planes. Whenever I saw -- I don't know when they were flying. Whenever I saw one I tried to run as fast as I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is: Did you hear or not that on the 24th, a plane was shot down over Vukovar, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Who could I possibly have heard that from? I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you heard nothing on that day or the following day, did you ever hear about something like that later on?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are just stories, planes being shot down and all that. Your people were shouting one thing, the other people were shouting something else, and people were saying different things. I knew nothing save for what was happening in Sajmiste where I lived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is no, you never heard anything about that later on?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's all just hearsay and stories. I didn't see this. I can't confirm it. I can only say no in answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that on the 25th of August, your wife was called to the hospital for an emergency. If my understanding is correct, from that day on, she no longer returned home, she stayed in the hospital and worked there. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's true. She received a call, an ambulance came along to fetch her, they took her to the hospital, and they had 24-hour shifts. Whenever she was able to come home, she would call me. I would go and pick her up and then I would drive her back to the hospital, and we kept doing this for as long as we could. When I fled Sajmiste I stayed at the hospital. This was sometime in September or early October. I'm not sure about the dates. How could I be sure about the dates? This wasn't exactly yesterday, was it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that wasn't my question. You answered more than I asked.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's just for you to understand better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I understand you correctly, you say that even after that date, your wife worked 24-hour shifts but whenever she could, she would go home?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: She never came home and stayed there. After she left, she stayed at the hospital. Whatever free time she had we spent together and we drove back as often as we could. But there was a time when we were no longer to drive back home and then she remained at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that sometime in July you became a volunteer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain how you did that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like that. We were called to the municipality, the old Vukovar municipality in Radiceva street. That's your local commune. There was shooting at the time so they organised for all the women and children to be taken away from Vukovar. My son drove them in a PIK bus to the island of Krk. Secondly, we were ordered to watch the houses of those who had fled, to shut the gates, and to try to make sure the houses were not looted because those people were our neighbours, after all. That was our assignment. There you have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you much like all the others, guarded the streets and the houses. Were you carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only had domestic weapons, the sort of thing that citizens wear. There were several hunting rifles and there was one Kalashnikov. I'm not sure where they got that one. We had small-calibre ammunition only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The transcript doesn't reflect that -- the fact that a Kalashnikov was there. Could you please tell us about that. Where did it come from?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was ten years back. I gave a statement ten years ago. I can no longer remember as well as I used to. It was maybe a pump-action rifle or something like that. I'm not sure it was a Kalashnikov but it was no major weapon. We didn't even have a proper automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that period, you went to the hospital to visit your wife?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever stay at the hospital with her during this time?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the specific period of time and how long?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was either in early October or mid--- I can't remember. Perhaps it was late September. I can't remember, but I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened there? How did you leave the hospital in October?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened, everything was shattered, that's what happened. The windows, the doors. Sime the driver who wasn't driving a car -- and it was all shattered. And then we got some planks to board up the windows so that there wasn't too much draft for the sick and the wounded and so people could keep on working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, my question is, after that stay in the hospital you left the hospital. When and why?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when I left the hospital? I left the hospital after I had stayed for two or three days. Three or four men came along and told us that we had to leave, those of us who were selected, Selebaj, Bilic, who else was there? I don't have a clue. Stanko, Sremac. Who else was there? Beats me. There were five of us but I know exactly what you're driving at. You mean about the palace? They took us to the palace and they told us we had to stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that time on, until the fall of Vukovar, you stayed at the palace?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that your assignment and the only position that you manned?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we left it only if we went to visit somebody, for example, if I went to visit my wife and we could go back to our houses but we were completely unarmed. We didn't even have a sling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, were you a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What military police? All of this, the ZNG and the military police, all that came about later, and I said this in 1995 when I gave my statement. We were nothing. We were not soldiers, we were not officers. We had no insignia nor ranks, we had no captains, majors, nothing. I don't know what we were. Well, I didn't carry anything on me. I don't know what other Croats did and now you're blaming me for something I don't even know for what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, I'm asking you whether you were a member of the military police, manning the palace, because this is what your wife stated here.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were called. I don't know how she learned this, how she heard this. If she heard that this was military police, then, yes, fine, you can write it down. I was a member of the military police. Fine with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the palace or perhaps prior to you going there, were there any major incidents, any instances of killing, either of the people who were there or civilians?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you the truth now and I hope the Court will listen to me. The greatest thing of importance there were the works of art, plus the five of us, Stanek and so on. We were all of different ethnicities. One was a Slovak, one was a Ruthenian, and so on. So we represented their brotherhood and unity. That's what we were. And there was another guy who was a Serb there, Stanko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will wait for the interpretation to finish. At one point in time, while you were there at the palace, or perhaps prior to that, did you hear that a large number of people were killed, let's say 12?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than that. Now you're talking. Now you're talking. I was hoping that you would put this question to me. It will take some time for me to answer. I apologise. We were there guarding the castle. There were large wine cellars below the castle belonging to Pik company, and then there was an opening where people went to get air. Otherwise, they stayed underground. They had candles, and we stood there guarding them. We knew if the candles were blown out that they would suffocate. Those who didn't drink wine, even those were drunk. And what happened then? There was shelling and I'm not sure but I think it was the Yugoslav People's Army, large shells were landing, eight bombs called Krmaca landed. One fell in front of the church. One fell in front of the gate. And they were as large as gas cylinders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whether was that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late October, sir. They kept firing at the palace and they kept yelling, "There are so many Ustashas, so many ZNG members. We will get the whole municipality killed."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were broadcasting that via loudspeakers. They asked us to come to the wood market and raise a white flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You're speaking about October. Do you know what happened at the palace in August or were you not there at the time?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, first I went to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, do you know what OSA 3 is?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear that. OSA is a wasp; it's just a little bit bigger than a bee. I don't know what it means where you come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same thing. Do you know if there was a checkpoint at Sajmiste?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have a checkpoint. I told you what we had. We had a local commune at Sajmiste. That's all we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember a school called Stjepan Subanc [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's right where I live, at the top of the hill. That school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there something there, a checkpoint perhaps?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing whatsoever. I was there, there were all these streets, Dalmatinska, Istarska, Slavonskih Brigada, and I don't know their names. These are narrow streets. As I told you yesterday, this is a small area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you don't know that such a checkpoint existed?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you passed there frequently, you don't know that such a thing existed?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no inscription, no sign saying so. Had I read a sign, then I would have been able to tell you so. But I didn't see anything and I'm telling you only about things that I saw and that I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you gave your particulars, you said that you had completed your JNA service.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Slovenia, in Tomlin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That at the time that lasted for 18 months; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Surely you remember that at the time when you were doing your military service, you also took an oath?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like the one I did hear except a bit different, in a different place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember at least a portion of that oath?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to refresh your memory --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I'm not about to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me try. This oath stipulates that those who take the oath would defend territorial integrity of the country.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wasn't at the time when I took the oath.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What country was it then when you took the oath?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was Yugoslavia, and nowadays, it's Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say nowadays, you mean 1991, the events that we are describing?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Croatia is a younger state, younger than Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, do you remember, and I can refresh your memory, that while Yugoslavia existed, the president of the Presidency was Mr. Stjepan Mesic?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and you didn't want to let him in so he never was the president of Yugoslavia. And now he's the president of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But Yugoslavia existed at the time, it was a recognised country, and Croatia still wasn't, if we can agree on that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how long it existed. It was Yugoslavia and then it split apart and then you started -- you started taking parts, and then Tudjman had a row with somebody and I don't know how this came about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now turn to your arrival at the hospital on the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that you stated yesterday that Vukovar fell on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know this? Based on what? Given that you were still at the Eltz palace on that day.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. Stanko Sremac, on the 18th in the morning, came and said, I'll go and visit my apartment. He lived in skyscrapers near the Danube. He had an apartment there and went to see his apartment. He went to see his apartment and didn't come back that night, the night between the 18th and the 19th. Where he was and what he did, I don't know. In the morning, he came, maybe it was 6 a.m. or I'm not sure; it was dawn. And he said to us, "What are you waiting for here? The army is at the Vuka River, the JNA soldiers and their weaponry, all of them are at the Vuka. Don't stay here. You can go to the hospital and find salvation there." And then he said to me, "Bule," that's what they used to call me, he said, "Bule, if you want, Drago, you and I can go to the Danube. There is a Hungarian boat there and we can take that boat." I didn't go with him. Rather, Stanek Rasidemujl [phoen] and I went to the hospital and we stayed at the hospital. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So based on that, based on his words, you know that the day before you went to the hospital, that is the 18th, Vukovar fell?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was outside. I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you or perhaps did somebody else tell you at the time that on the 18th, the Mitnica defenders surrendered to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, don't ask me that. Sljivancanin was in the hospital on the 18th in the evening and people disappeared from up there, and there was a major in the hospital who went around with a nurse looking at the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never mentioned the 18th.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you got me all confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's try and answer this in an orderly fashion. Please wait for my question to conclude before you give your answer. Can we agree that based on what you learned on the 19th, upon arriving in the hospital, nobody had come into the hospital prior to that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The JNA troops and officers entered the hospital on the 18th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that that was on the 19th, in the evening. You came on the 19th in the morning in the hospital and there was nobody there.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unable to see anybody because I went straight down there. There was nobody I could see. I could barely see myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You came to the hospital on the 19th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While en route to the hospital, did you come across any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were all moving at the same time. There were walking around like hordes with sacks and looting and stealing everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you came to the hospital and you said you were unable to enter through the back entrance?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the main entrance and through the emergency entrance, yes, that's right. We couldn't go through those entrances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was locked?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Locked or something else. I don't know. I couldn't open the door and I wasn't about to break it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you came to the main entrance and you couldn't go through that entrance either but the glass on the door was broken so you were able to enter that way?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This is a large door with two parts, with glass, and it was broken so this is how we were able to come in, the three of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you were waiting there to see your wife, were there a lot of people there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't mention this. There were wounded people lying on the floor, on the stretchers, civilians, everybody was there. It's an unimaginable sight. One cannot conceive this. There were so many people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say there were a lot of people. In your statement, you mentioned the sons of Mr. Kolak?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. They were my neighbours. There were three brothers, two were killed, the father was old, and I don't know whether he is still alive. They lived on another street close to me called Patkoviceva [phoen] street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you said that you saw them changed into medical uniform, that that surprised you.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they were defenders of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you explained how you acquired a white coat. You said that your wife gave you one.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please wait for me to finish my question and then confirm it or deny it. So based on the request of your wife, Mrs. Kolesar gave you a white coat?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that you became a part of the medical staff?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't. I didn't have an ID saying that I was a doctor or something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The staff, the people who worked as auxiliary personnel, who did physical labour at the hospital, did they wear white coats, blue coats, or green coats?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of coats they wore. I saw that people with white coats had IDs. As for the labourers, how would I know? I came to the hospital, I greeted my wife, there were people in white coats around me. How would I know? What was I able to do that? You can laugh all you want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are not laughing, Mr. Bucko. Far from it. I'm asking you what labourers wore, the auxiliary personnel. Did they wear blue coats unlike medical personnel who wore white coats?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, you know very well, one knows well who is a doctor, who is a nurse, and who is a labourer. I don't know what labourers were dressed in. If nurses were unavailable then drivers would help carry the wounded person inside or outside. And how were they supposed to be dressed? They had to have some kind of a uniform. They couldn't go in their outdoor clothing, all dirty and then help with the wounded or the patients. Don't ask me this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, I'm trying to ask you about what you know. What I know is irrelevant to the Trial Chamber. It's not me testifying here. I'm asking you about all these things, no matter how clear you think they are.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: What was the blue overcoat about and why were you given a blue one? Did that mean that you would be evacuated with that blue overcoat on?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way, no way. I was wearing the white overcoat because I was dirty. Ever since the shelling began in July, I hardly washed and I had nothing to wear. If somebody saw me I was quite a sight, without meaning to offend anyone or myself. She was thinking about what to do with me, Biba, I know her, I know her husband, she knows my wife. She was thinking about how she could help me so she found a short, white coat. It wasn't even big enough to fit me. It was big enough for a child perhaps but not for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned your friend Kolja, that's Mr. Kolesar, Mrs. Kolesar's husband?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we agree he was a member of the National Guards Corps?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea what he was. He never shared that with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A correction for the transcript. Mr. -- Mrs. Kolesar's husband, because originally it said something else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said and your wife confirmed that you had spent that evening in a room off a corridor where there were many wounded and sick lying all over the place.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you said you hardly slept a wink that night?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: And who did? Who do you think could have slept?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't interrupt my question. Wait for me to finish my question and then you can speak. Did anything happen during that night or was that night quiet at least?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was all sorts of things going on outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking about the hospital and the corridor?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were the wounded. We were in this small room, the sterilisation room. There were some shreds of cloth there and dirty linen, that sort of thing. We were waiting for the end. We were waiting for the observers to come. We were waiting for the evacuation to begin. Who was there? My wife, Magda, Ilonka, and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely why I asked the question.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just you go ahead but please don't try to lead me astray.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following morning, the 20th, did anyone come to your room?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the morning. I have no idea. It was still dark. So I really didn't have a clue. I suppose it was still in the morning. A man came over, he must have been a soldier, I guess. He banged on the door and he said, "All of you to the plaster room, now." We were surprised and I stayed there alone. He said, "You can't stay here. We'll lock you up." I was just standing there looking at him and I said, "I can't stay here. I want to go, too." And he said, "But you can stay here." And then I came out of the room, and I walked a little. I have no idea whether they locked the room up or not. I think that it was locked because when I came back to get my coat it was locked. That's how it was. And then everybody went to the plaster room. So there you have it. That's how it happened. On the way there, or, rather, as I was walking back, or when I left the hospital, well, all sorts of things were happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife went to the plaster room and you went out -- you went out. You put on your blouse after that and --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, no, no, no, no, no, ask away, ask away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time ask someone to call your wife who was in the plaster room to go back?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was walking towards that room in my poor coat. I came to the room, found that it was locked. I saw Stanko there and I asked him what's happening. Because I saw that those two soldiers were driving everybody away. Selebaj was there. That was his last name or first name, I don't know, with his wife. He said, "Where is Mara?" He said, "I don't know." I said, "Go look for the key," and then she went off and came back with a key.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this because you didn't say this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You just go ahead and tell me what I said and what I didn't say. I can confirm or deny for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you talked to somebody else, not her.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But that was later on, when I left with the coat on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did see your wife. She left that room, she gave you a key. This is not something you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me. If you had asked me I would have told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that back then, in those conversations that you had, you always indicated that you were a civilian and you demanded to be or expected to be evacuated alongside with everybody else.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It wasn't like that. You can say whatever you like. We just took those coats in order to carry the wounded. That's why we took the coats. We wanted to help the nurses carry the wounded. What could I possibly have done there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm talking about. You indicated that, were you in fact a civilian or did you consider yourself a member of the ZNG, military police, or any other unit?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a civilian. I felt a civilian. People knew that I was not a help worker for the hospital. Everybody knew that. It was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to briefly go back to Kolak's sons, the people you mentioned. Your statement seems to suggest you were surprised to see them and that it was wrong of them to act the way they did. Is my understanding correct of that part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain why you thought there was no way to treat people or was there a different reason?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way they treated people was no good. If they had been heroes up to that point, and they gave us the coats, everybody knew we didn't have the ID. You weren't blind. Of course, you could tell. Some people had long coats but you knew they weren't doctors. He just came there and somebody gave him this coat so that he can help carry the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one final thing. You didn't speak about that yesterday and you did say that in your statement, so I would like to remind you now. Back at the hospital, did you see Marin Vidic, also known as Bili?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see him, and the other one that you didn't ask me about, the main man at the hospital. The name escapes me. It's on the tip of my tongue but I can't seem to remember it for the life of me. Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you knew Marin Vidic, Bili, you knew who he was?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I knew him. He was the main man in the municipality at the time, the president of municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know who was president of the municipality before him?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Krpina, Dokmanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why and how Marin Vidic, Bili, was at the hospital that day?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was the president of the municipality, probably he was there to arrange things with the other people. He had a right to be there but I'm not going any further into that. None of my business, is it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When on -- did you see him or on what occasion? Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 18th in the evening, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bucko. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for asking me all these questions. I'm truly, truly glad that you did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am glad that you are glad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While everybody is glad, I think that Mr. Borovic has a few more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He may as well go ahead, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Borovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. There will be a handful of questions, that much is certain. I'm Borivoj Borovic, counsel for Mr. Radic, Mr. Bucko. I will start with this last question. You said that on the 18th in the evening you saw Marin Vidic, Bili, where was that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are you doing there on the 18th in the evening when you said several times that you only arrived on the 19th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 18th, the 19th, well, I may have got it mixed up. One day was supposed to be on the 18th but, no, no, no, it was on the 19th and the 20th. The whole thing was happening because you were trying to get me confused on this one yesterday. So I'm getting the numbers mixed up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't the one leading you astray yesterday.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but someone was and that's why it stayed with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what's your answer? When did you see Marin Vidic, Bili, the last time?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 19th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What else were you doing at the hospital [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know? What are you asking me for? You should be asking him this. I have no clue. We weren't mates or anything. How should I know what he was doing at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the hospital did you see him in?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corridor. He was on his way out of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On his own?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he and Bosanka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where they went to?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know? I didn't ask them, did I?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go back to the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When exactly was the defence of the town first organised? What do you know about that? When were you first informed that a defence was being organised?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organised? Town? My street? July. It started in July. We were called to the local commune because that's how it was. We had to do something about the shooting that began. Serbs were fleeing Vukovar. We had to watch their houses. We had to send our children and wives off on a bus, that sort much thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those of you who weren't Serbs organised yourselves and sent your children and wives out of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I wasn't even there when they saw them off. It's the local commune. They were the ones who organised this. I wasn't there, and I wasn't the one who drove them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So Croatian children were being seen off --

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, don't talk like that. I'm not going to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think the witness should show some respect and allow me to finish my question. Please hold often a while.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Listen to me now --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The children who were moved off in the buses by the commune, Mr. Bucko, can you tell us who those children were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Who were they.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were children, citizens of Vukovar. Please, it has nothing to do with Croatian children, Serb children. Nobody was thinking about that. Don't try to make it seem like it was like that. We lived as brothers and sisters until the very end. I spent ten years in exile. I've had enough. I'm sick of these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we've only just begun.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I can't go on like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question: Where did these children go? Where were they being sent when this was organised by the local commune?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard they were being sent to Krk and some of them returned. I have no idea who came back and who didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is my understanding correct that Serb children went to Krk and that this had been organised?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Serb. Everybody who wished to go could go. Nobody was forced to go. Whoever decided to send their children away did so. There is a slant to your questions that I don't like and you're trying to make me answer your questions in a specific way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were those children Croat or Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you it was all mixed. Nobody was separating Serbs from Croats or Serb children from Croatian children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave my child alone?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your child, whoever's child. Don't do it like this. You're very aggressive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question: Did the local commune have a plan that they shared with the men from Sajmiste, a plan for men, for adults?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What plan are you talking about? There was no plan. There was an arrangement, there was shelling, bombs were falling more or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was an arrangement, who made this arrangement?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Menges Zlatko, one; his son, two; Kelava Mirko, three. They were all there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they organised this meeting and they ran the meeting?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't the organisers. They were members of the local commune. They had to be someone in the local commune who was a member to send out invitations to people, that sort of thing. What else they were, what their positions were, I have no idea. They were my neighbours. They happened to be there. I have no idea what else they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before the armed clashes, in your best estimate, how many Serb houses were there in Sajmiste and how many Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: More Serb than Croat but not the whole of Sajmiste, just my area of Sajmiste. There is no need to hurry like this. How do I know how many people there were? There was Petrova Gora, too. That is also part of Sajmiste but it's called Petrova Gora what do you say about that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome, very welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your area how many Croat houses were there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea. I didn't make lists of people. I know that the judge was there, the teachers were there. The municipal workers were there. They were all Serbs, holding positions. Nobody talked to them. Nobody said you are Serbs so that's why you have all the positions. I came there in 1970. I was the youngest member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your statement to the investigators here in The Hague and you confirmed this yesterday, as well as today, in answer to a question by my learned friend, Mr. Domazet. You said people started leaving the Serb houses and you remained there to watch the houses so they weren't looted.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the Serbs leave their houses or what?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'll tell you. It was like this. Some of them left their houses, left altogether and never came back. There are those who left their houses at the time and came back later on, and there are those who left when we left. They saw us off. They greeted us upon our return and they are still together with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did they too participate in your defence units in Vukovar or not?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who, those who stayed? Well, I'll tell you. It was like this, Rajic, Pero, son, he's in Novi Sad. He's my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't return after the war?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand did they return or not?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sons didn't return and their father and mother stayed there. They saw me off when I left and I found them when I got back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Croats leave your street at there period in time too or not?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a joke. So you don't know.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a simple man. How should I know? Most Croats were expelled from Vukovar. I can list all of them for you, those who live on my street and around my street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't ask about later. I was asking about this period of time when you were still in Sajmiste and when Serbs started leaving their houses. My question was: Were Croats leaving their houses too?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that organised defence began. Organised by whom?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: By no one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are just trying to trick me. I know what you're trying to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Units in which you were, did any in them wear uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nothing?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing they were all civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Would you please describe to us how Sremac was dressed?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same as you and I, or rather not you but same as me and everybody else who was there. I apologise. You are really asking for details. Perhaps he wore a bear's fur but I don't know. I mean, don't you a laugh at me. I don't know what you're doing. You're trying to make a fool of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not doing that. You're doing it yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I understand my learned friend has to cross-examine. I understand the difficulties, perhaps more than most, but it's getting to the stage now where the witness is just being upset, in my submission, perhaps unintentionally, and it doesn't do the whole Tribunal any good at all vis-a-vis the evidence. I wonder if my learned friend would no longer laugh at him. I understand it is difficult sometimes. But it does show an element of disrespect and, if he wants respect back, it has to apply both ways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. I would say to all counsel that this is a time for quiet calm and patience. If we are going to get answers and we saw that both Mr. Moore and Mr. Domazet were able to and you already have made some progress, Mr. Borovic. It's a matter of quiet, steady patience and you may hear a lot more than you had intended to hear when you ask a question, but somewhere in there, there will be the answer to your question. And I know that this is difficult for Mr. Bucko. It's not something he wants to go through in detail. And he's having difficulty with the process of being asked again and again about things that he doesn't see to be of much use to anybody. We might see it a little differently and he will, I'm sure, try to understand that. But if we can just quietly plod away, I think you might get what you need and eventually we will be able to reach the end of the evidence. Could I ask counsel, though, particularly as three Defence counsel are cross-examining, to really think about the matters they are questioning about. Are they important or not? Have they been dealt with enough already? Because I think unnecessary repetition, and unnecessary probing into small side details, will only delay the whole process unnecessarily and not get any of us very far. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm not going to argue with you, but the Prosecution should be careful about what witnesses they bring here. Perhaps they should have been prepared to withdraw this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Borovic. The Prosecution have obligations to bring witnesses, whether they like them or not, whether they are going to further their case. If they further your case, they should bring them as well. So the Prosecution don't have a freedom of choice about witnesses in our system. Understand that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Your Honour. Thank you. We will carry on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were taken to the palace of Count Eltz, who did you find there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You made a mistake. I wasn't taken there. I went there myself. I went myself to the hospital and also to the Count Eltz palace. What do you mean was I taken there? You speak my language but you're twisting me and then I will tell you in Croatian that I'm unable to answer such questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on what your wife said and what you said to the investigators, they came to fetch you, to take you?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the hospital.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the hospital, yes. I thought you meant from the palace. You should turn to me, act like a man, not laugh at me, and look me in the eye when you're talking to me. You're smarter than I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is your answer to my question? When you were taken to the palace of Count Eltz, who was there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who was there? The palace was empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it locked?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It had been broken into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there something in the palace?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some works of art. There were some valuables, and I don't know what else. I wouldn't be able to estimate there. Whenever I went there I visited that place as a museum. That's my answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said certain things were broken. What was broken?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was shelling, you know that there was a war going on, so what do you think one could find there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were there things broken in the palace or around the palace?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you how many Krmaca bombs landed there, before and after. They kept shelling the palace because they said that Ustashas were there and the ZNG members so they were just shelling away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will never get an answer because you are not treating me properly. I will not answer your questions any longer. Nobody will force me to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So what pieces of art did you find there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, valuables, pieces of art? Well, what we found there, statues, paintings, you know what one can find in a museum. Don't ask me what was there. How would I know? I wasn't an expert on museums or anything like that. You know everything but all you're doing is shaking your head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is where were the valuables located in the building?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the building, it wasn't on the lawn. Please don't ask me such questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, is there area of questioning of any real relevance in this case? The witness says it was a museum. He was asked to guard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, but there are facts indicating that at the time it wasn't a museum but, rather, a military facility. This is why I'm putting these questions. I want to verify. We know what with we have in our evidence and I want now to hear the witness. We want to know whether he was there as a soldier or as somebody guarding pieces of art.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Borovic, why don't you put to him your understanding of what was there, if it's different from his statement that it was a museum? I don't think you're going to get very far asking this witness about works of art and collections of valuables. You see?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see everything, Your Honour, but I'm trying to ask questions in such a way as to prove that this witness did not guard any works of art but was there as a soldier. And in order not to put leading questions, I'm going -- I'm trying to go step by step. I can put an end to such a procedure but yes, I understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What he's saying, we were there guarding museum, but there weren't great valuables there. There were people there under the museum, in the cellars.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you left the palace, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. What do you mean we left it? We haven't left it yet at that point. Sir, these bombs were not landing only while we were there. They were landing at other time as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a mother there with two children, wounded, and a grandmother was killed. A lot of dead people that we pulled out of the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please answer my question?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not going to answer anything and you cannot force me to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not answer his questions any longer. He is attacking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, I think the problem is that you are seeing a lot of things in wrong way. You are -- Mr. Borovic is trying to learn from you some things that only you know, and you very quickly --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You very quickly lose patience with him. Now, I can understand that you find all this process very difficult, but you, as I told you earlier, you will help us, the judges, a great deal if you try to listen to what Mr. Borovic asks and try to give an answer where you can. Now, you may not be able to tell him anything about works of art or valuables in the museum. And you have told us that there was shelling in the area, and you've told us that people who were in the cellars or the cellar were injured, but Mr. Borovic now is wondering, when you left the palace, did anything that you see happen to the palace when you left? Can you remember anything about the palace when you left, anything particular?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I left the place, there was -- there were many people slaughtered there in the basement. I don't know how many were wounded. Children. There was a massacre there. Mother, children were wounded. Two daughters. And grandmother was killed and then the wounded people were taken tout. I don't know how many. They put them on a trailer and took them to the hospital. Their last name is Vidic. That's what happened. I don't know if the gentleman heard this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I didn't hear it so I doubt that Mr. Borovic did. Is this from shelling or some other cause, that all these people were injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Krmaca bombs that landed on the palace and around it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This was before you left the palace, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before, certainly. All he's trying to show here are the valuables and me there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you left the palace, what was the position about the people who were down in the cellar? Were they still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what happened once I left the palace. I don't know what happened there. Once I left the palace and after that was gone, I know that there are some witnesses in Vukovar who are alive, eyewitnesses, and perhaps the gentleman could go and take a gift to them. These were the JNA shells.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The people who had been in the cellar sheltering, were they still there when you left the palace? Or had they gone already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. This was a team collecting the wounded. I wasn't involved in this. We -- if you went to the basement, then you could hear. You could hear people crying, and then you would know that something had happened and this is what we were actually guarding. We were guarding the hospital, and we were there to ensure that these people were all right and if somebody was wounded we had to send a word, you know, because we couldn't just leave the people there in the basement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean to say a moment ago that you were guarding the hospital or were you guarding the palace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were guarding the palace. And the people in the basement, those who were in the basement, those poor people who were killed and who have been scarred for life.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you yourself went to the hospital on the morning of the 19th of November, were there still people in the cellar, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Once I left, I don't know. I came to the hospital on the 19th in the morning. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned you were there to guard the palace. Were there others helping you guard the palace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were only five of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were any of these members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None, none. We were just ordinary civilians. We had a hunting rifle and something like a pumping shotgun. I don't know. And then when we stood guard, we would swap weapons. So the only time we left the place was when we went to visit somebody. I went to the hospital, Sremac went to his house, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were there any members of the MUP there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Borovic, I've asked a few questions round the area that might help you to see where it is you need to ask anything further on that subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour. Based on all previous statements and testimony, I learned that the task of this witness was to guard works of art in the hospital [as interpreted]. My question was whether they took the works of art that they were tasked with protecting from the palace when they left it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you could, yes. Mr. Borovic and I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We took no valuables with us. I don't know if there was anything that was of value there. I saw no Picassos. I really wanted to see a Picasso painting. And then my wife asked me after the war, where is your Picasso now? I don't know that there were any valuables there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's a good answer. My next question: When you came to the hospital [as interpreted] you said there was no one there?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no one. It was the -- the war was broken down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So there was no one there. What month was it?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was October, early October, or a bit later. That's when I went there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So nobody there. The door was broken down, the palace was empty?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everybody fled because of the bombing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So when did this people arrive, the ones that were in the basement?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. When I got there, I don't know who looked after them. There were civilians there. I don't know who was looking after them. We were just told that we should help each other. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Following the directions of the Court, let me try and put it this way: You said that you went there in October and there was nobody there. And now you are saying that there were some people there that you were looking after. When did they come and when did you start looking after them?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know when they arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If one looks at the transcript, and I'm looking at line 16, page 37, 16, there is reference to when you came to the hospital. You said there was no one there. And then there is reference to October. It may well be that there is a misunderstanding in relation to whether one is talking about the hospital or whether one is talking about the castle.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- my apology. I think it's a misinterpretation. The question was about the palace, not about the hospital. You're entirely right. Can this be corrected, please, the line in the transcript? We weren't talking about the hospital. We were talking about the palace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I thought that it was just a mistake when it appeared on the screen. Mr. Bucko, you might be able to help me with that. When you first got to the palace to start guarding it, were there people already sheltering in the basement, in the cellar of the palace? Or did they come later? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't. I can't remember when they arrived. Once we had arrived, we heard children call or cry, I'm not sure how I should put it. Then we realised somebody was there and then somebody came up and said, "There are wounded people here, there are men and women lying on benches." Who was responsible for that, I don't know. And then he comes up and tell us, let's take care of this and that. He was our boss. We had agreed. That's what we did. He was going around checking what should be done and what have you. Once or twice we changed the candles because the gas could explode.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You left the castle on the 19th, not taking with you any valuable works of art. The five of you leaving the hospital, do you physically see these people you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's just off the road. You don't seem to understand. The distance is the same as between me and the judges. That's the road and there is the Danube. There is a tunnel there, a cellar, wine cellar, God knows what, God knows who built it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But did you ask any questions about what happened to those people that you had left behind? Did you just leave them like that?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Leave them like that? What do you mean? What became of them? What are you trying to say? We are -- when Sremac came up and told me to go, I went. There was nothing else I could do. He was outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think it was recorded in the transcript that Sremac was the commander.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please speak one at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript should reflect the fact that Sremac was their commander. I don't want to make it seem like I'm trying to manipulate the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Sremac your commander or not?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander, commander, he was an educated man and we were trying to agree who would write things down. Of course it was him. He was one of us. He lived with us. We shared the same pension, we worked in the same company. I'm telling you so you know what this was about because you're saying he was with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, was Sremac your commander?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What commander? What are you talking about? He was an ordinary person just like me. We were just trying to agree on what would do what. What commander are you talking about? There was no captain, no major. He was just an ordinary guy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they took you to the Eltz palace, who gave you the weapons and when?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What weapons are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The weapons that you had.

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the man who came with us brought the weapons. I don't know. There was a hunting rifle and that other thing, what's it called? You use the same sort of ammunition as you do for a hunting rifle. I only saw those weapons for the first time there and then. I had never used weapons, not even in the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Those people who came to the hospital to take you to the Eltz palace, they had weapons on them, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have weapons on them. What are you saying? They brought along from somewhere and then God knows what. Don't tell me they had weapons when they were in the hospital. That's the -- that's the mistake about you. You're talking about weapons all the time and you just wouldn't listen to me. How can a civilian just be there? I told you those people were all civilians, how could they just walk into a hospital carrying a weapon? Who would have allowed that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, my next question because again you failed to answer my questions. When did they bring those weapons?

utterances.speaker: IRINEJ BUCKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was 15 years ago, my friend. 15 years ago. How am I supposed to know who had brought the weapons and who hadn't? When we came there we knew what was in store for us. Please don't try to make me look stupid. I'm sorry, I have to put it like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, I think you are not listening very carefully to what Mr. Borovic says. You are --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't. I need a break. I can't keep listening to him any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, probably that's not a bad idea for all of us. We'll have a break and you can just calm down. But when you come back, if you could try and listen to Mr. Borovic's question. You seem to jump from his question to something a little different and imagine he's putting something to you that -- he really often isn't doing that. So once you've calmed down, you may be able to hear him more clearly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Your Honour. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for trying. We will adjourn now and resume at 10 minutes to 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you very much. Your Honour, there is one matter. I've asked the witness to remain outside in case he understood what was about to be said. I hope you don't mind. It's quite simply this. I've spoken to one or two of my learned friends at the break. They have indicated concerns about the translation this morning. And I think it's right to say that there has been an indication certainly by Mrs. Tapuskovic that they well ask for an audio tape and perhaps a retranslation of the video. Now, that is entirely their right and their prerogative. The only matter that I would be concerned about is quite simply this: If there is a problem with translation, and I've already spoken to the interpreters upstairs in OTP, we have a view, and I say it straight out now, that there are some errors but not significant errors. But if there is going to be an issue in relation to translation, in my submission, it should be dealt with now. If there are any ways that the matter can be resolved, and I would have perhaps thought the way the witness behaves, he explodes, I have savoured that delight in proofing, then it may well be that he can be asked to slow down or the interpreters ask him to repeat the -- whatever he is saying.
