I'm open to any suggestions or any directions from the Court. But I do feel with the utmost respect it should be dealt with now. It's not a case, so there is no misunderstanding on this from Mr. Borovic's point. This is not a case here of a witness where we say that he is incredible or not believable. We say he is credible and believable, if a little rustic in the way he approaches things but it's not a case here of feeling obligated to call a witness that we are suggesting or submitting is unreliable. So I just raise the point in my submission it should be dealt with now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I would like to clarify the exact nature of the exchange between Mr. Moore and myself during the break. Mr. Moore approached me and asked me about a comment that Mr. Borovic made on page 26, line 1, when he told the witness, please leave my children or my child alone, after a witness made a comment about children in general. So he understood that it was Mr. Borovic's children that he was talking about. Mr. Moore asked me if Mr. Borovic has any grown-up children or child and if maybe this child was involved in the war. My answer was if there are any doubts about the interpretation, we also have the audio tape, the audio recording of today's session. There was no implication whatsoever that the Defence would be asking to have the tape reviewed or to manipulate this against today's witness. After all, our cross-examination has not even been completed yet. That's the extent of this story. My friend Mr. Moore said he didn't understand the answer that Mr. Borovic gave but in our language, and in our understanding, the comment made was about the witness not being supposed to involve Mr. Borovic's children in this whole thing. So that is all that Mr. Moore and I spoke about. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: My learned friend is absolutely correct about the reference about "did you leave my child alone," I think is the phrase that was in English. Clearly, if there is a personal element one is concerned about it and I certainly did ask for clarification in relation to that. I consider that to be a perfectly proper approach. I in no way am suggesting that Mrs. Tapuskovic is trying to maneuver or manipulate in any way at all. That is not my concern. If my learned friends, and I use the collective, are concerned about the translation, I would submit it should be mentioned now rather than later on. It is not just a case of one phrase, and I repeat, I'm not suggesting in any way at all that Defence are trying to manipulate. I just want to make sure that there are no mistakes in relation to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think we are wasting time. I think we are on the right track to complete our cross-examination, thanks above all to the patience of the Trial Chamber. There are no objections. There are similar -- there are a number of details that require further clarification. We can go back to the transcript later on. If the witness is ready, as far as I'm concerned, we can just go on. If the witness is not prepared to go on, then I have precious little else to say. Every witness has an obligation to respect the Court, just as we do, the parties. If the witness is prepared to reappear in the courtroom now, I suggest that that should be done as soon as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Can I make a couple of things clear? First, that comment, which has concerned Mr. Moore, was one which, as far as the Chamber is concerned, is merely one of a number of curious expressions in the course of various flows of language from the witness and from -- between the witness and counsel, which we take at the moment as of no particular relevance or significance at all. And it will remain that way unless there is in truth some more fundamental issue behind it which needs to be aired. It is clear that in the case of this and for that matter any witness, that it is quite easy for there to be some error in the transcript. It occurs because largely of the speed with which both the interpretation and the typing has to occur, and it's no particular fault of anybody, but if there is some matter which is of importance that appears to have gone wrong, we have already, I think, got into the routine of raising it at some convenient moment so that the strange or unusual answer can be checked with the witness and the matter clarified. That way we can avoid any ongoing problem and get the situation sorted out while the witness is here. I've got to express my admiration for the way in which the interpretation service has coped with this witness. It is very difficult when the witness reaches the point where he feels he must intervene and talk over counsel so that two people are speaking at once, and when he speaks at the speed which his emotion drives him to speak with, how anybody has been able to keep up with that is something that is almost beyond my appreciation, and I'm very grateful for the efforts that have been made. Can I suggest for all counsel, as it seems likely that this will be the pattern of evidence from this witness, that the moment he bursts in, there is little point in trying to stop him until he has poured out whatever it is. If counsel just stops speaking until the witness finishes, I know it's a reversal of order but I think it's the most practical way of us eventually getting through the questions that counsel want to put and hopefully getting an answer from the witness. And it will give the interpretation and the transcript-typing people some hope of recording the essence of what is being said. I don't think I can usefully add anything more at the present time. We all appreciate that there are difficulties in handling this witness. At times when an impasse appears to have arisen I've tried to step in and get the witness receptive to more questions again, one way or another, and then allow counsel to carry on. I hope that by one means or another, we can reach the end of the witness's evidence with counsel having achieved what they need to achieve with the witness. If the witness could be brought back into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Borovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bucko, for waiting. There are a few more questions from Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard that there was an underground passage going to the Pik basement. My question is: Is that the same basement as the basement of the Vupik company?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Vupik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself go to that underground tunnel?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go further than the place where the wounded people were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, namely that the shelter which was below, which was the basement of the Vupik company, was linked underground with the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made back in the times when the Turks were here. I don't know what was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that this was an underground tunnel?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long is it?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see it -- all of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how far in the tunnel did you go when you saw these people?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you then describe this underground tunnel to us?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no light there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please explain it to us?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I describe that? There were wine barrels and there was a small passage. I don't know. I didn't work in the wine company. People lay there on the floor. There were just these huge wine barrels and civilians there were drunk from the odour of wine and whenever they got out they were killed. So people there were killed and there were wounded. There was a storage and -- outside and whenever they got out they were killed because when you got out you got hit by a shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you quite say?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the shells didn't pierce the tunnel. Don't interrupt me. They didn't pierce the tunnel. It was when these people went outside to get some air that they were killed. When they went outside they stayed in a shed and this is where they got killed. The shells didn't pierce the tunnel. There was a Krmaca bomb that fell right in front of the entrance to the palace and then one landed in front of the church and these bombs were as big as gas bottles or gas cylinders. That's how big they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May we continue?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any of these people inside the palace or did they just stay in that passage 100 metres away from the palace?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was nobody in the palace but the five of us. Don't thank me. Wait for me to complete my answer because otherwise you'll complain that I didn't answer you correctly. Don't treat me that way. Please take your share of responsibility. I took an oath and everything I've said so far was true. You are guilty, all of you killed so many people there. Now, after 15 years, I have to go back to those events and what do you think how I felt while you were shelling me, and now you're doing this to me again. Please don't do that. You have no character.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this a good time to warn the witness? Perhaps this would be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, I don't regard the matter in the light that you do. But, Mr. Bucko, what is very clear to the Chamber is that you are wanting to view these proceedings as involving some personal attack on you and the memories which you hold dear to you of people who may have been killed or injured. There is no intention on the part of this Court, and as far as this Court has seen, no intention on the part of anybody taking part in it to personally attack those memories which are very dear to you. It is necessary, however, for counsel to ask you some detailed questions about some matters that may involve some unpleasant memories for you. Now, they are not doing that just to provoke or upset you. They are doing that because it is of importance to this case, and, as I put to you in the beginning, we have to learn about this case from you. And we therefore have to ask you to be understanding when questions are put to you and to try and be patient and deal with those questions even though they may offend you or hurt you. They are not being done to offend or hurt you. They are being done to try and help the judges here. And we would be grateful if you could try and understand that, and try for the moment and just listen to the question and answer it, and not think about so many of the things that are upsetting you. Now, the quicker we can deal that way, the quicker the questioning can finish and you will not have to put up with it any more. So if you could try to see it in that light and just get on with answering the questions, the quicker you'll be able to get away and get back to your ordinary life. It's not giving Mr. Borovic any pleasure to be having to ask you all these questions. He's got a job to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Eltz palace, was there a warehouse of military medical material?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military medical material? I didn't see it. I didn't hear anything. To tell you the truth, I don't know what there was there. I only went to one room but I didn't see any traces of that, and I myself didn't take any of the stuff that was there and that's in line with my upbringing. That's the kind of man I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the five of you had a weapon issued to him?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of us. We didn't sign a receipt for any weapons. I don't know when these weapons arrived. All I knew was that I guarded one door and the other person guarded the other door, and then we put our weapons, the hunting rifle and the ammunition, on the table. That's where we would find it. There was nothing of the sort that you are implying, no army, nothing of the sort. I don't know why you're bringing this up. They never set foot there, your army or ours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the war, in view of the fact that you were a member of this formation, and I'm not going to specify which formation, did you receive any benefits, any retirement benefits, or any veterans' benefits?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have 35 years of service and I never got anything else. Why are you saying this? I don't like what you're saying. All you're trying to do is shift the blame on somebody else and disregard your share in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please give us the names of these five people?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sremac, Stanko, Irinej, Bucko, Selebaj -- no, not Selebaj, Stanek. Just a minute -- oh, darn it. There were five of us, just a minute, please. Mandic. There was Mandic. And another one, Vasas, yes, the five of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the two Kolaks were they there?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. They were in the hospital. Don't mix them up with this. There were just the five of us in the palace. Sremac came later. The four of us came from the hospital and I don't know where Sremac had come from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would are the Kolak brothers?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: My neighbours. There were three of them. Their father, Kolak, worked with me in the same company, if you really want to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take off their uniforms and put on -- hospital clothes on?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was nothing of the sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If -- and if I tell you that on page 3, line 5, you yourself mentioned the Kolak people and if you want I can give you this to read it, and you said, "I remember seeing the two Kolak sons wearing these uniforms. I didn't think it would help anybody."

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't see them in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. And prior to that, you said that you were disappointed because they had changed their uniforms took them off, and pretended to be hospital personnel. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did so, dear sir, and I stand by it. As for the uniforms, if they had uniforms, then, yes, I can confirm that. Let it be the way you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put Exhibit P59 on the ELMO, please? Thank you. Could we zoom in, please, the downtown area. A bit more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question for the witness: This is a map of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it by heart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please show on the map the area where you were at the time, the palace of Count Eltz?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's got to be here because the Danube is right behind it. Here is the Danube.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please put a cross on that spot?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be around here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please put a cross on the spot where the palace is?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the colours are a bit difficult for me. Let me tell you. The Danube runs right next to it and then there is the Vuka River. It's by the church. Around here. Around here. Because -- around here. The church and the cross, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you please draw an arrow towards Danube and write in number 1?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So that we don't get confused on this map. So from this spot would you please draw an arrow towards the Danube and then write number 1?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not how it was. That's not how it runs. The Danube is here and the Vuka is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Not the hotel. I mean the river.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the river, but there is a hotel there now as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it slowly, just write number 1 here.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Here is 1. And here is number 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please erase number 2, we don't need it.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to erase it. I've never done this before. I've never even seen something like this before. You people are asking too much of me. Why don't you come to Vukovar and I'll show you where the Danube is?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please now circle number 1?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Circle the Danube?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Circle number 1.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the map? Well, here is the number 1. Here is where the church was and this is where it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please circle the number that you wrote, not the church, the number?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't do that because it's front of the building. The Danube cannot be on a road. How can it be on a road? The river always runs behind a building, the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be erased, because this is quite messy on the map and it will be of no assistance further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please put a dot and then circle number 1? Otherwise it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're trying to convince me, I don't know where the river is. I don't see all these dots of yours. I'm 63 years old and now you're asking me to do this. Don't be too smart. How do you expect me to do this? I don't know. All right. Well, let's erase this. All right. So this is the Vuka River and then the Danube. And here is the cross, the church and this is where the palace is. I don't know how else to explain it to you. And now I'm expected to put a number 1. You know all these things. The army was in Vukovar. Of course, you know this. You know that the Danube is behind it. The Vuka River used to join the Danube. It doesn't do so any more because it's been cut off, and it flows in this direction. And this is where it flows into the Danube, right here. And I can put number 1 there. This is where it flows into the Danube.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't ask you this and I think the Chamber expects us to give up.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. You are doing all this to make it look that I need to give up but you don't know where the Danube is. You can't even show where it's on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, unfortunately, the Chamber has not been to Vukovar. Now, I think what we might do is just wipe clean everything that's there, if the Court officer could do that. Thank you. Now, would you be able just to put one red dot where the Vuka --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you be able to put next to that a number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you draw a small circle around the number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we understand from you that the Vuka has now been closed off from the Danube. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Closed off, because it was dug over towards the end, there is a circle there now, but still, there is a very small stretch where it flows into the Danube. It has the same thing as before but it's very short. It comes out right here and then it goes right underneath and then it comes out here. But this is the main thing, this is the main island, just across the way, and it should be around about here. This is the rowing club. The rowing club should be about here. And then there is the hotel now. What did it used to be? I think a fishmonger's shop or something like that. That's the stretch of the river. This is the Vuka and this is the road leading just past it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was the Vuka cut off before 1991 or has that happened recently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was cut off -- I was still working. They dug it over. I was still working. When was it? I don't know. I was working at the Vuka on the river-banks of the Vuka and the Danube. I can't remember the year but I was there and I was working too. That was my company. Nobody can tell me now where the Danube is. I know it by heart. I can just draw a line here and that's that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that was well before 1991, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Dug over, Danube. Nothing was done, nothing. That was before. Not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, was there any other point you wanted marked?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That was my intention and I never asked anything about the Vuka, to begin with. He spoke about it of his own accord.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the witness now, please, mark the location of the Vupik company?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here the palace is, the castle. That's where the Vupik company is. And then across the road from there, you have the Vupik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark that, please? Put a dot there to mark the exact location of the company.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it now. There is a road leading here. This is the main road, right, okay, so these are the buildings, not facing the Danube because the Danube is the other way. This is in reverse. All in all, it's in front of the palace across the way from the palace, not the hotel, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is off mic. The interpreters can't hear him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The building is right there. So there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please be so kind as to put a number 2 next to that dot and circle it, please?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please indicate location of your house?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's impossible. It's off the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we zoom out, can you please show us the general area of Sajmiste?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's try. This is the road to Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been informed, Your Honours, right now that we can't zoom out right now. We'll have to make a new exhibit then, I suppose. But while we are at it with this map on our screens, can the witness please show you us which road to the hospital he took on the 19th, if we can draw that on the map.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's right here. This is the road I took, right here. The hospital is right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and draw a line from this number 1 here to mark the route?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, but I think this is right, this is the number 1, I went here and passed here but it's difficult there and then I went here and here and here, following this line, the Danube is at the back of the hotel and here I am right in front. So it's about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please draw the line as far as the hospital, please?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't distinguish these. This can't be. This is too small for me. I can't see properly. I just can't. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I respectfully make a suggestion? Firstly, the witness perhaps to wear his glasses, and secondly, there is no dispute as far as the fact --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I might as well put them on, yes. No problem at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Mr. Bucko, can you just keep quiet for one moment, please? There is no dispute where the hospital is. Should the witness not be told where the hospital is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where it is. I'm telling you, I don't know where the hospital is. When I take the road when I'm there, I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I asked you if you could find your way around this map. You said you could.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but a proper map, the sort I keep in my car. Not this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see this thing here that says hospital on the map?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do I know what hospital is? You should show me a photograph or something. I have no clue. I recognise the letter H. When I'm in a car, when I drive, I use a map. I can find my way, but this is too small.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm trying to help you, Mr. Bucko.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no way you could possibly help me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to be patient. Where it says hospital, that's the hospital?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I suggest, Mr. Borovic, that we receive as an exhibit the present markings and then we may be able to change the zoom and that may help the witness to see a little more clearly. So we'll now receive the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: With the numbers 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you like us to get to a bigger display?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just have an ordinary map, the sort that civilians use? I really don't understand this map. Can I just have an ordinary map, the map that I can use, the map that I keep in my car to drive around? I have no idea about this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in a little now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's it. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, you need to zoom in further so that he can see more clearly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is the hospital to the right. But the Danube is not between the hospital and the Pik company. Oh, Christ, yes, it was the Pik after all, and the palace was there. That's what is leading me astray, the hospital and the palace and the Pik. You're trying to lead me down the garden path. You know, when I left Vukovar, ten years ago, how can I be expected to draw all the details for you and meanwhile you're laughing. I am no longer prepared to allow you to go on laughing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not laughing at all.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure you're laughing. I went to school in Vukovar. You're telling me about Vukovar, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we've had about enough of that. If you see the photograph that shows you the hospital, there is an arrow pointing from that photograph to a red dot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the road. The main road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you see the red dot at the end of the arrow from the picture of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, that's where the hospital actually is, where the red dot is. Okay? And can you see the main road? It's in a sort of orange-brown colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can't be. The hospital can't be on the same river-bank as the Danube. The hospital is to the left and the palace is to the right. If you're taking the road to Borovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe that's the witness's answer. I'm trying to establish his credibility, and this, too, goes to the witness's credibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I really question that we are going to gain a great deal pursuing locations on this map with the witness, Mr. Borovic. He clearly --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He's clearly not oriented to this type of map.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I do believe, however, that based on the answers provided by the witness, above all to my learned friend, we might acquire an impression. I asked him about the location of his house, to please indicate that for me. If he can find his feet or not, I don't know. I'm prepared to help him along. It is not my intention to confuse the witness. But first of all I have to check whether he was at the Eltz palace at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I was. That's what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can Mr. Bucko please draw the location of his home on this map?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't, using this map. I'm not very good with this map. I don't know this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that is the case, I believe that maybe he could.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can but not with there sort of map. I've never seen a map like that before. This is the very first time I'm looking at a map of this kind. You know the sort of map that you keep in your car. If I can be given an opportunity to use that, I could show you the hospital, my house, the road, but I've never seen this one before. I've never seen this map before. I wasn't trained to use this sort of map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You completed secondary education?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, gymnasium? Secondary education? Yes. Agriculture. I'm not as clever as you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The briefing notes say secondary school.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's a vocational school, three years -- for three years you are trained to do a certain type of job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was an error, we should correct that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was certainly not a gymnasium.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's an error on the part of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Must be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I appreciate your patience.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, finally the witness lass told us that he's not able to use this map. Therefore I'm withdrawing the remaining questions concerning the map. We now no longer require the map for our purposes. We can remove it from the ELMO and just move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you were friends with Sremac?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friends? What friends? We weren't friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I knew him. He worked for the pension fund and his wife worked for -- at the hospital. She was an employee there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he live in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He lived at least two kilometres away from my place, up on the hill. I just don't know the name of that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the three other people that you mentioned in answer to my question, were they from your street, from your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not one of them, not one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How, then, do you explain the fact that during all this time, you just guarded your street, you organised yourselves?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're trying to confuse me. You know when I came to the palace. I don't need to explain this. I stand by my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. If you'd be so kind we'll try to move on.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You and I, we can't move on. This trial may as well go on for another 15 years. You and I will never be getting on well. I'm trying to give you my answer and you're trying to confuse me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear. None of these five people were from the same street. Can you then explain to the Trial Chamber the fact that you, of all people, were chosen at the hospital and you agreed to go, the five of you. Who could have forced you to go there and watch the castle?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might have been an old lady with a sling for all I cared. No one forced me. They said, "You've got to go there. You've got to guard the palace." And that's what I did. I went there and that's what I did. What could I possibly have done? I spent all that time all over the place so I thought I might as well go and guard the castle. What was in that castle or palace? Nothing, after all. It was open, like I told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's my question. Did the five of you go of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the five of us. It was myself, Stanek, and Vasas, and Sremac came later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the fifth person?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same thing. I'm not sure when, give or take a day or two. It might have been one day earlier or one day later. His name is Mandic. You want to know who he is? After so many years you're asking me. You know there is no way for me to know. But you're shoving me along any way. What I said the first time around I'm still saying the same thing and what I'm saying is the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told the investigators here in The Hague, and you repeated that today, that for you, who came from the Eltz palace, the hospital was the place that offered you the boast chance of survival. My question is: Why did the hospital offer you and your pals from the palace the best chance of survival? That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're not listening to me. I said Sremac came along and said to us, on the street, that the army was at the Vuka. What are you waiting for, he said, I said that in my statement, I stand by my statement. I don't wish to repeat myself any more. Whatever I said in my statement is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Why did you believe that the hospital offered you the best chance of survival?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ask Sremac. Track him down, ask him, "Why did you tell Bucko and the other people, 'I'm going to my place, I'm taking a boat into Hungary.'" You should ask Mr. Sremac what he said. He's a much cleverer man than I am. He probably knew why he was saying that but I have no idea. You should go and ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps ask him why you would be going to the hospital and why that was the best place to be?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: We parted ways at a street corner. We didn't really exchange too many words. We weren't chatting like old ladies, like, how are you, how have you been? Did you have a good night's sleep, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question: So what became much your weapons when you ran away from the palace?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I've been waiting for. There you have it. It wasn't too long coming. The weapons, we put it next to -- we put it next to the cash register there so that it may be found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What cash register are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know the ancient kind, made of iron, the huge cash register, the sort they used in banks or a safe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the ammunition there too?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we just dropped it right there on the floor, just so it wasn't on the table where it was visible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you what happened to the Mitnica group. I'm asking you a different question. Have you ever heard of the Mitnica group?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no groups. I don't know anything about any groups. From the 7th on until the -- from July on until the fall of Vukovar I just watched my house. I guarded my house. Please don't keep attacking me like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after the war, did you hear anything about the Mitnica group?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? I didn't see anyone so that I could talk to them about it. I've been in exile for nine years, how could I have heard about this Mitnica group? I have no idea who those people were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your wife said that she wanted to lock you in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of a habit. That's what she used to do at home. I never take any keys with me so she always used to lock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, my question was why did she want to lock you in?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that I wouldn't go out because they were telling her to go to the plaster room and she wanted me to stay there. She wanted to lock me in but she didn't lock me in. I got out. And then she took the key. I don't know where the key was. Selebaj lady knows where the key was and then my wife came and gave me the key and she said the soldiers are outside, and I told her you are shut in in the plaster room and then I will have to go. That's what I told her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you entered the hospital, you said that you tried entering through the emergency entrance. That's how you described it. When you came to that entrance was there anybody standing in front or inside?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: The personnel was there, patients. How would I know after 15 years who stood there? I entered like everybody else. There were no soldiers, nobody else, just soldiers and patients.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So on the 19th, there were no soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came on the 19th in the morning. That was one thing. And when the army came, that's another thing. The army came on the 18th and then on the 19th your army came, because evacuation was supposed to take place on the 19th and 20th. But nobody came. You're not trying to say that, are you? You're just trying to pinpoint the 19th, the 20th, trying to trick me. I've had enough of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise but I really did not quite catch your answer to my very clear question.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. It's very clear, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did I understand you right that you said that when you came to the hospital on the 19th in the morning, there were no soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No soldiers in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait. Wait. But on the 19th, they came in the afternoon. In the afternoon, the 19th. That's what happened, sir. Your Chetniks came. And then on the 20th there was an evacuation. You are trying not to mention your Chetniks. And I will put an end to that. From now on, I will only give you yes or no answers. That's enough. I've had enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I continue, Your Honour? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you entered the hospital on the 19th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you how many. Stanek, Vasik [phoen], I and then the two others. I've said this 15 times already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Mandic went?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you. He and Stanek went to his apartment, the skyscrapers near Pik, there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that there were any members of the ZNG in Vukovar at the time?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. I heard that in Zagreb because they started gathering there in a place where we were, the people were there without documents. We had nothing. And we started gathering there. The first time we got together was when we gave the statement, when people were supposed to give statements for this Court. This is when people got together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just stop for a minute? You said that you gathered in Zagreb for testimony. What testimony are you mentioning?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: A testimony about what happened in Vukovar, sir. To say why we had come to Zagreb, to say that we had been expelled, driven from our homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you give your statement?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb. It says so, in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this when your wife gave her statement?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We gave it together. I don't know whether she went first or I did. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you give a statement here in The Hague after that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: To whom? No. This statement that you have is your statement. I didn't give no other statements. I just came there, and I was questioned before it began, the testimony, just to check whether everything was true so that I wouldn't look silly in the courtroom. Nothing else. I don't know how else to describe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I truly do not understand you.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you don't want to. I don't know how to explain the process to you. What do you mean? You know, do you think that I can just come in and testify before being prepared for that? That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they suggest to you what kind of answers to give?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come on. I don't understand you, even throw we speak the same language, and it's easier for me to understand the people who speak a different language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So you gave a statement in Zagreb and then you gave another statement here in The Hague. Did you sign the one in The Hague and did you sign the one in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed the one in Zagreb, but I didn't sign anything in The Hague, and they had to put our names down that we were the citizens of Vukovar. Here I didn't sign anything. They treated me nicely, like a guest. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What year was it when you were here in The Hague, when you came to confirm your Zagreb statement?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year it was in The Hague? Well it says there. In Zagreb, it was in 1995, and in The Hague is right now, when I'm standing, sitting in front of you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You probably made a mistake. You meant 1995.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1995. Yes. You drove me mad. So no wonder I made a mistake. I have to answer your questions but everything I've stated is the truth, and I stand firmly behind it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us conclude with this: You gave a statement in Zagreb. Did you give any statements here in The Hague to The Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just talked to them like human beings. They asked no statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: My learned friend has asked questions and he's been working on a premise that is completely wrong and not on the evidence given. This witness was said -- or was asked, "Did you give a statement in The Hague?" I think it's at page 68, and he said he did not give a statement in The Hague. My learned friend then went on and then said, "so you gave a statement in Zagreb and then you gave another statement here in The Hague." He did not say that. So the question is based on a false premise. It's an error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. I think we've reached the point in the last answer, the witness has made clear that he made a statement in 1995 and that he came to The Hague this year now to give his evidence, that he was not asked to make another statement, and he didn't make a statement in The Hague. And I think that's where Mr. Borovic's questions have got us. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right. Thank you. If that's the answer that he came to The Hague only once and that this is the occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Zagreb you gave a statement with your wife?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with my wife. We did it individually. Not together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Individually but on the same day?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know. But we didn't receive the invitation to go on the same day. Not on the same day. I don't know if it was on the same day. But I didn't sit together with her. The kinds of things you ask! I can't tell you whether it was together or separate. I don't know. But let's be the way you want it to be, together. We are husband and wife, after all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that on the 2nd of May you were in the hospital when the wounded from Borovo Selo were brought in.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at the hospital. I was in front of the hospital, going to meet my wife, because I'd been called in to bring her some food, and I was informed that the wounded were brought in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were --

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in front of the hospital, not inside, because I was just arriving there when I saw the wounded. I was not inside, not indoors. I was standing outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you enter the hospital on that day?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I hardly did. I don't know what happened. You want me to describe the events of that day, and how would you feel if -- if you lost so many people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you to come to the hospital on that day, and why you?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know as much as you do. That's how much I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow for the -- that it was -- is it possible that you were called from the National Guards Corps to come in?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. Don't try to get me to say something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that I should come in and bring food to the hospital because the war was expected in Vukovar. Why are you fooling around with me? Are you trying to tell me that we were making love at the hospital as they were bringing in the wounded?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Serbs among the wounded or, rather, do you know who the wounded persons were? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I know? They were being brought in, the regular people. They were regular uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of uniforms they wore?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what regular police uniforms look like. They are blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you asking? Do you think I was looking for the insignia?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay on the 2nd of May?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably know it better than I do. I don't know anything any longer, how long I stayed there, but I'm sure you do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that starting from July you were engaged, involved in what was going on in your streets, in your area. Were you doing your duty with weapons or not?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What weapons are you talking about? In July, the kids had their school break. The schools were out. We had to look out for children to make sure that they didn't get killed. Stop asking me about this war. You are guilty and just stop asking me about this. Your army is guilty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your area, how many members there were of this civilian protection, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Man, you're trying to tell me how many people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how many people?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five, six, ten, it was a small street. Not longer than 500 metres and other streets were as long. There were three streets and then we didn't know what was happening elsewhere. As for the whole city, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In all of these streets that you mentioned, were there members of civilian protection in all of the streets?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called them civilian protection, and I stand behind -- by it. They were ordinary civilians, ordinary people. That's what they were. And this is why you sent them to Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to guarding the empty Serb houses, what other tasks did you have?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just to help, to help, and what weapons? What weapons are you talking about? We had no weapons in our local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that a witness who was located in another headquarters, in Mitnica told us that everybody from civilian protection was armed, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armed, all of them?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What witness said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you say to that, is it true or not?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people I saw had no weapons, and I have no idea about the people she saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome, you're quite welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of the 204th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zagreb. All of us got together and this is where we heard about all of these stories of yours, the ZNG, Chetniks and so on. They wrote about us as though we were a regular army, and there was no regular army but for your army. There was your army there. And our people had not even taken an oath or anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that you did not have regular Croatian army in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No regular army. We had no such army. No army that was organised so that we had a Lieutenant, a sergeant, a major or so on. We had ranks, no ranks. People had to earn -- to earn these decorations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that what you had was actually a paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What paramilitary? I don't even know how to answer your questions. I don't know what you are asking me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If I tell you that your wife, who testified here before you, told us that you had weapons, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Weapons? Do you know when we had weapons? Let me ask you, what weapons? My wife doesn't know what a weapon is. She never saw any weapons or anything. A weapons, if we had a rifle, then it would only be a hunting rifle that we wouldn't be able to take outside before 10 in the evening. The only thing one could see in the streets were civilian weapons but no automatic weapons. How was my wife able to see a single piece of weapon? People were not -- did not dare go out during the day with any weapons, only after 10 in the evening. It was not that type of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the palace of Count Eltz, did you go and visit your wife at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever I could, I would go behind houses and get to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she ever go to visit you at the palace?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no way, never. Nobody came to the palace. We were the only ones who went outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then how was she able to say that you had weapons?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the guards -- don't interrupt me. I told you. Don't interrupt me. You're trying to take me astray. You know what we did in town? We guarded your houses and your houses are still standing there to this day. And regardless of that, we treat you with respect. And you're not treating me with respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I continue?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. As long as you want.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a nurse called Binazija Kolesar?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, the head nurse at the hospital. No, surgical ward or the hospital, I don't know. She is an older woman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question, direct one: Did you ask her, through your wife, to put you on the evacuation list?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask that. My wife did. My wife asked her. I didn't ask for anything. How was I able to ask her for anything when it was my wife who was a colleague of hers and a friend, so how would I come up to her and ask her for a coat? Don't say such things. I didn't ask that and I stand firmly by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you put on that list, the evacuation list?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you saw it, I saw it. They said the evacuation people would be there, the Red Cross, that they would be evacuating people, the wounded, nothing else. There was nothing else that I could do but bring the beds outside or the stretchers and that was all we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if your wife made a list at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that. I wasn't at the hospital. How should I know? They were in the plaster room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were there on the 19th, 20th and 21st?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not in the plaster room when this gentleman introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you're beating about the bush. Why don't you ask me a direct question? I was helping the wounded, there would be an evacuation, we going or not? What's with the barracks? Off we go, and that's it. You're just trying to fool all these people who don't really know what happened. That's all you're trying to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that your wife had made a list containing the names of 60 [as interpreted] ZNG members, including you? Did you hear about this later on?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were the first to tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a mistake in the transcript. I said 16 and not 60.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16. I'm not sure if that's what it said. You're saying this. But I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if there was a joint command for all these local communes that were organised to offer protection across Vukovar's neighbourhoods?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear sir, I never went to any other local commune but to mine. It was right there in front of my house. That was in our neighbourhood. That was our block. Those were the people I knew. I walked all over the place. I passed all the streets but I didn't see a thing. This is all I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of Tomislav Mercep?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later on, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What precisely did you hear about this man?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a hero of some sort or something. What do I know? A civilian. They kept saying, "Mercep, Mercep," but I'd never laid eyes on the man. Perhaps somebody could tell me. Was he in Vukovar? Where was he in Vukovar? What did he do? These are questions for him, not for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Who asked you about the 204th ZNG Brigade in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: What 204th are you talking about? What Brigade? Nobody asked knee about the brigade. They asked me about what had been going on in Vukovar. Please try to remember this. There was no ZNG, no Ustasha. The question was: What happened in Vukovar, where were you, what did you do, how did you manage to survive?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you a while ago about the 204th and you said you were asked questions in Zagreb about that.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not asked questions. They were talking about it. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was talking about the ZNG and the 204th, what you're suggesting?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody from Vukovar. People were talking about it. I'm not sure who came up with it first. Please, don't press this because I have no idea how this came about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In September and October, did you at any point in time hear about the fact that there were passes being issued to people in Vukovar limiting their movement and that these were designed by Mercep?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm hearing it from you first thing. I know nothing about any passes or permits or anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear about HOS members in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. Now, when they're showing movies on TV, what you're talking about, the HOS, they are showing it on TV now but I have no idea who those people were. I'm watching it on TV now but I didn't see it at the time. They are playing movies all over Croatia. We know all about you, just so that you know, sir. Not only Mr. Sljivancanin, but there is a photograph of his. He is putting a shell into a barrel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About I didn't ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you're beating about the bush. I'm telling you so that you know. You're firing questions at me and I'm about to start firing questions at you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I hope it's verbal firing we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, words, words, not verbally, words, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you're both very practised at it. Is that the end, Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately not so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you have very long to go?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 15 questions to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have a break now, then, I think. We'll have another break now and resume at 20 minutes to 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour, I'm sorry to have to deal with one matter again. My learned friend has put a question to the witness which we have now located. It's at 76, 13, the question is, "Did you ever hear that your wife had made a list containing the names of 16 ZNG members, including you?" That is wrong. The wife's evidence has been checked over the break and in our submission that was not said in any way at all. It's on the transcripts page 2729, there was some cross-examination on behalf of Mrksic, and the question that was asked after some evidence had been given and it reads as follows: "Thank you, Mrs. Bucko. You said that you took a piece of paper and you had the pen why your pocket and you put names on that piece of paper and you also said it was about 15 to 16 names." My learned friend, Mr. Borovic, then in his cross-examination, took the evidence -- I'm sure unintentionally shaped the evidence in a way as follows: "Thank you and if I tell you that he had reason as a member of the ZNG, which is indisputable now, even according to what you said to hide in the hospital, so that the JNA would not arrest him, can you confirm that?" So there is various references to the list, but the evidence that was given was that Mrs. Bucko in her evidence said she did make a list, it was because of the concerns about their husbands and there was no reference to the ZNG whatsoever. Now, it may well be my learned friend will submit that that was a ZNG list; he's perfectly entitled to do that. But in my submission, it's another example of him inadvertently putting to a witness evidence in a way that is incorrect and it is unfair, putting it neutrally. In our submission, if he's going to put questions like that, he should put it accurately and properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore. Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure about the general meaning of my question. I know the lady spoke about the 16-people list. I know that it was in the context of hospital employees. I'm not sure if any other witnesses perhaps provided this information, that they were ZNG members. If the Prosecutor likes to have it this way, we may as well call them 16 husbands. We shall use other evidence to prove that they were ZNG members, all of them. We do have some evidence about that coming. The question was perhaps slightly inaccurate. But if that is all right, I could repeat the question. There were no particular intentions that I had at the time. I asked a simple question about the list with 16 names and I was expecting perfectly straightforward answer, Your Honours. My apologies. I believe I even said something like, Did you ever hear that she had made a list with 16 names on it? I left an opportunity to the witness to comment on my question with no strings attached. At any rate, I can repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Borovic, I don't think there is any need to. The answer that's come has been very clear. This witness had not heard of that list or any such list so there is no need to go back over that. It is a matter that all counsel ought to take notice of, though. If there is to be put to a witness evidence from another witness that has been given, it needs to be put correctly. There, as has been pointed out, are significant differences between what was put here and what was actually said by the witness. That is not going to advance anybody very far in this case, and I would ask counsel in future to be careful that they -- if they are quoting the evidence of a witness, to get it right. And then we won't have any misunderstandings or other difficulties. So I think we can put that matter behind us now, and move on to your remaining 15 questions, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can the witness then please explain to a certain extent I've already introduced him to this subject, what exactly he told the investigators? He said that afternoon I saw some of Vukovar's defenders wearing medical uniforms. "I was very disappointed that they had had a change of clothes and pretended that they were medical staff." My question is - I am here quoting the witness - why was the witness so disappointed just because Vukovar's defenders had had a change of clothes and had put on medical uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to answer this. I had this shitty rag on me and they had the same sort of thing, poor things. I said, "What use is this to you? You don't even have any insignia or anything." Of course, they understood they had nothing because all the hospital staff, the medical staff, had a badge or an ID. That's why I told them that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I really apologise but there is another question. You seem quite clear about this. "I was very disappointed that Vukovar's defenders had had a change of clothes."

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. Not the defenders, I never said the defenders, please don't insinuate, no, no, no, no, no. It wasn't about defenders that I was talking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can I have the usher's assistance, please to show the witness this B/C/S version? In the English, this is page 3, fifth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 3, fifth paragraph. In the English it's page 4, second paragraph. What it says about Kolak. You see the name there?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind to answer --

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please read out loud?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure, I will. "I saw some of Vukovar's defenders." You see what I mean here, I didn't mean soldiers, I just said defenders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please can you be so kind and obliged, do what I've asked to you do?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now you've got me side tracked again. It's difficult "When I came to the hospital ..." I skipped over this part. "After the fall, I saw some --"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's not what I'm saying. In the afternoon, that's what I mean, the bit that says in the afternoon. Can you please read this out in your own language?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the afternoon, I saw some of Vukovar's defenders wearing medical uniforms. I was disappointed, very disappointed, that they had changed their uniforms and were now pretending to be hospital staff."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to press this point now but does it not indeed say "Vukovar's defenders," like I said?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, "defenders." People who were defending their town, not soldiers. Do you see my point? Defenders, yes, but not the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on, please. This is quite sufficient for my purposes. My next question: Who is Josip Lovrinic? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: His wife used to work in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is he? It's not only his wife that distinguishes him, is it?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that. I never sat at the same table with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his occupation?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then explain how, in your statement, you state that he worked in the hospital's kitchen? How do you know that? You say you never saw him or knew his occupation.

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out on the bus, in the barracks, when your people herded us on to the bus and when your police officers were beating us, saying, what did you do at the hospital? We had the white overcoats on. And they were beating the life out of him and he said, "Well, I only cooked meat at the hospital."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know if you'd never been introduced? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he said it. The policeman had asked him and he said it himself. Of course I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Stanko Sremac? He was not from your area or your street?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he was your commander?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a headquarters or something like that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Sajmiste? Did you have some sort of a ZNG headquarters there and did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no headquarters whatsoever, just the local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Zlatko Menges is?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the headquarters located at his home?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no headquarters there. It's the house just across the way from mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the ZNG headquarters was in the school building in your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Josip Tomasevic, a.k.a Joso is?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the distance between the MUP building and the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP building is just behind the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the distance between the PTT building, the post office building and the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
utterances.text: The PTT building is near the Vuka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far?

utterances.speaker: Irinej Bucko [Resumed]
